- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a downward correction of 1–2% to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-1.0) within 3–5 days, model frequently underestimates the decline; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect sentiment-driven correction.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in capturing short-term sentiment shifts; if sentiment flips within 3 days, adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect new sentiment direction.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or positive; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average to avoid overextension.
- When sentiment is mixed (±0.5) or volatile, model often averages out sentiment; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast, avoiding extreme outliers.
